eval-bot: nightly-eval: model=redwood-llama-13b-qint8 variant=packedkv-2026-03-19 metric=task_hallucination rate jumped from 0.9% -> 8.3% on math-multi-step promptset. failing prompts: 142/1700. link: https://ci.redwood/ml/nightly/1976543209
sofia: who saw this? cc @maya @ben — looks large for a quant bring-up :eyes:
maya: I saw the alert. spinning up the failing sample set now. prelim glance: many responses start with a confident but wrong intermediate step (e.g., misapplied carry).
ben: is this the new tokenizer change we landed yesterday? I thought that only affected deterministic whitespace handling.
kai: I reproduced locally with the quant artifact (packedkv-2026-03-19). CPU eval matches hosted. 
sofia: repo + build tag?
kai: artifact: redwood-llama-13b:qint8-packedkv-2026-03-19, tokenizer commit: 9c3b7a, inference-runtime: 4.2.1
maya: quick diff shows tokenizer added an extra mapping for <NUM> special token (we wanted aliasing for ops pipelines). suspect: token id offset for one reserved token changed from 50256 -> 50257 in the tokenizer table.
ben: hmm that could shift embedding lookup by one if we didn't reserialize the embedding table ordering during quant. any sign in the logits?
sofia: attaching sample pair (prompt / generation).
sofia: ```
PROMPT: "Step-by-step: 58 + 67 = ?"
OLD (fp16): "58 + 67 = 125. Explanation: 58 + 67 = 125 because..."
NEW (qint8): "58 + 67 = 145. Explanation: 58 + 67 = 145 because..."
```
maya: interesting: internal tokenized prompt lengths match but outputs pick different tokens early. I dumped the first-token logits for both runs.
maya: ```
fp16 first-token logits top3: [(125_token_id, 12.3), (145_token_id, 9.1), (other, 1.2)]
qint8 first-token logits top3: [(145_token_id, 11.8), (125_token_id, 10.0), ...]
```
maya: suggests embedding->logit projection mapping mismatch rather than pure numeric quant noise.
ben: so hypothesis: tokenizer id shift + embedding serialization order mismatch during quant pipeline -> wrong embedding vectors assigned to token ids.
kai: I ran an alignment check: compare unquantized embedding matrix row i vs quantized artifact row i for the reserved region -> offset of 1 for indices >=50256.
kai: ```
# quick check
for i in range(50250,50260):
  print(i, float_equal(unq_emb[i], dequant(q_emb[i+1])))
```
sofia: that explains targeted failures on numeric tasks that rely on special token mapping we added. many math prompts include <NUM> aliasing exposed this.
maya: root cause writeup (short):
- Trigger: tokenizer commit 9c3b7a introduced alias mapping that changed reserved token ordering (added new mapping with new id 50256->50257).
- Fault path: quantization pipeline expects tokenizer.vocab -> embedding matrix index alignment; upstream token-id shift was not propagated to embedding serialization step. During qint8 packaging we serialized embedding rows in the original ordering while tokenizer produced shifted ids. Result: tokens mapped to wrong embeddings. Numeric/instruction tokens affected more.
- Why it shows up in evals: downstream math multi-step prompts depend on exact special-token embeddings to anchor reasoning chains; wrong embeddings produce plausible but wrong steps -> hallucinations.
ben: mitigation ideas?
kai: immediate: rollback to previous tokenizer commit for any production qint8 artifacts and redeploy canary to dedicated pool.
sofia: + add a gating rule in nightly-eval: if task_hallucination increases >1% absolute for any promptset, fail artifact promotion.
maya: + patch: make quant packaging re-derive embedding ordering from tokenizer.vocab at package-time (single source of truth). I'll open PR with tests.
maya: diff to add assert in packaging: ```
- # old: assume vocab stable
- assert len(vocab) == emb.shape[0]
+ # new: map embedding rows by token string to guarantee alignment
+ emb_rows = [emb[token_to_id[token]] for token in vocab_list]
+ assert emb_rows.shape == emb.shape
```
sofia: timeline: rollback canary within 1hr, block promotion pending gating, patch + unit tests by EOD, full repackage and canary run tomorrow morning.
tony: we'll also add a targeted golden prompt check: pick 50 deterministic numeric prompts and check exact answer equality for canaries.
ben: create a postmortem once root cause PR merges. add owners: maya (fix), kai (artifact validation), sofia (eval gating), ben (prod rollback).
kai: I've started the rollback job to dedicated-canary. monitor link: https://infra.redwood/deploys/1976543301
sofia: thanks all. please drop short updates here when jobs complete. :thumbsup:
kai: rollback complete, canary running, initial metric dropped to 0.95% on canary pool (within baseline).
maya: PR up: https://git/redwood/tokenizer/pull/412 — includes package-time alignment + unit tests + golden prompt checks.
sofia: marking this thread as ongoing until PR merged and gating enforced. good catch everyone. :sparkles:
